measurement: Net revenue recognised in the period
use_when: Any scorecard that touches selling. A Finance aspect without it is measuring something other than the business.
trap: Revenue by brand is not revenue by company. The source file's F1.1.1 is one brand's revenue alone; adding the brand rows together and calling the sum company revenue double-counts anything sold through two channels.

measurement: (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue
use_when: Positioning work where the point is to sell the same volume at a better price rather than more of it.
trap: Carries the same unit as cost-to-revenue and the opposite direction. This pair is the whole reason direction is a stored column: no unit and no name tells you which way the metric runs.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet BSC 2025 — target moved 56% to 57% with the reason logged

measurement: Total operating expense in the period
use_when: Any block that owns a budget rather than a revenue line.
trap: Scored target/actual, not actual/target. Spending 1223952 against a 1752681 plan is 143.20%; the higher-is-better formula returns 69.8% and inverts the meaning of the year.

name_vi: Tỉ lệ chi phí trên doanh thu
measurement: Total cost / net revenue
use_when: When the argument is about efficiency and absolute cost is expected to rise with volume.
trap: Moves when either side moves, so a good month of revenue improves it without anyone spending better. Read it beside operating_cost, never instead of it.
source: Structure read from BSC_2025_template.xlsx; direction confirmed by the accounting-reclassification note in sheet Explaination

measurement: Planned COGS minus actual COGS as a share of planned
use_when: Manufacturing and sourcing scorecards where the year's plan is an explicit saving.
trap: The source file's 2025 target for this moved because labour cost was reclassified from account 641 to 627. The 2024 and 2025 numbers are not comparable, and a chart that draws them as one line is wrong even though both figures are right.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Explaination — Target 2025 is 57% with save 1.5% COGS

name_vi: Giá trị tác động truyền thông
measurement: Launchmetrics MIV assigned to every brand mention across press social and KOL
use_when: Brand-awareness objectives where the deliverable is coverage rather than a sale.
trap: Denominated in money and it is not revenue — adding it into a financial total inflates the year. It is also very noisy: one unplanned mention by another brand moved Hanoia's month enough that February was excluded from the 2024 actual, with the reason logged — which is why an actual needs a raw figure, an adjusted figure and a reason, not one number.
source: Launchmetrics MIV definition; BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet 2024 row C1.1 stores actual 685000 / target 561600 = 121.97% and types 1.2 over it, while sheet Explaination gives the adjusted 80600 + 609000 = 689600 / 561600 = 122.79%

measurement: People who recognise the brand / people surveyed
use_when: Category-entry work where nobody is looking for you yet.
trap: A survey number with sampling error. Store the sample size beside it or 80% of 20 people and 80% of 2000 people print identically and read identically.
source: Standard survey definition; the source file stores the percentage without a sample size

name_vi: Tỉ lệ đơn hàng thủ công mới
measurement: New-craft SKUs ordered / total SKUs ordered for the coming collection
use_when: Product-launch objectives where the mix is the point rather than the volume.
trap: Raw achievement was 147.50% against a 10% target and somebody typed 120% into the cell. The non-financial cap is 100%, so the hand-cap was wrong in both directions: wrong level, and invisible to any audit because the raw figure was overwritten rather than kept beside it.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet 2024 row C2.1 — 0.1475 / 0.1 = 147.50% overwritten as 1.2

measurement: Count of resellers signed to distribute in a new market
use_when: Distribution objectives where each unit is a negotiation and the steps are not linear.
trap: Scale, not ratio, and in 2024 the two disagreed: rungs of 0/1/2/3/4 against a target of 3 put the 100% rung at 4, so an actual of 3 that met the target scored 75% on the scale and 100% as a ratio. The file typed 100%. The rung table was the thing that was wrong — a scale whose full rung sits above its own target is misaligned, and hand-typing over the output hides that instead of fixing it.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet 2024 row C3.1 — target 3 actual 3 rungs 0/1/2/3/4 at 0/25/50/75/100/120%

measurement: Count of artist collaborations developed and proposed to Buying
use_when: Collection-development objectives where each collaboration is a discrete win and partial credit is real.
trap: The clean scale row in the 2024 file, and the reason it is worth keeping beside resellers_acquired: rungs of 0/1/2/3/4 against a target of 4, actual 3, scores 75% on the scale and 75% as a ratio. When a scale is aligned to its target the two formulas agree, which is exactly why a card that only ever tests an aligned scale never discovers it has the branch wrong.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet 2024 row C2.2 — target 4 actual 3 rungs 0/1/2/3/4

measurement: Count of logged customer complaints
use_when: Service and quality objectives once volume is high enough that zero is not the expected value.
trap: Falls when logging gets worse as readily as when service gets better. Pair it with a leading KPI that counts contacts, or the scorecard rewards a broken intake form.
source: Direction taken from the guideline list of lower-is-better metrics in BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Guidelines

measurement: Clicks / impressions
use_when: Channel work where the creative is the variable and the spend is fixed.
trap: Cheap to move and easy to mistake for a result. A creative that doubles CTR and halves conversion has made the number better and the business worse. Never state a causal claim from CTR.
source: Platform-standard definition; graded a heuristic because its link to revenue is not measured by the metric itself

measurement: Acquisition spend / new customers acquired
use_when: Paid-channel scorecards where the question is whether growth is affordable.
trap: Money-denominated but not booked in the financial statements, so whether it takes the 130% financial cap or the 100% non-financial one is a decision the organisation has to make. The source file does not answer it. Graded non-financial here as the safer default, because the lower cap cannot inflate a bonus.
source: Standard definition; the cap question is unresolved in BSC_2025_template.xlsx

measurement: Total revenue / total marketing spend
use_when: Blended-channel reporting where per-channel attribution is not trusted.
trap: Deliberately unattributed, which is its strength and its limit: it says the whole engine is working, never which part. Do not cascade it to a channel owner as a personal KPI.
source: Standard direct-to-consumer definition; named in the source file's KPI Warehouse sheet

name_vi: Lợi nhuận trên chi phí marketing
measurement: (Gross profit from marketing - marketing spend) / marketing spend
use_when: Budget decisions where the alternative use of the money is the real comparison.
trap: Needs gross profit, not revenue, on the numerator. Substituting revenue turns a losing campaign into a winning number and the error is invisible in the output.
source: Standard definition; named in the source file's KPI Warehouse sheet

measurement: Customers active at end of period who were active at start / customers active at start
use_when: Subscription and repeat-purchase businesses where acquisition is already working.
trap: Defined by the window. Monthly and annual retention are different metrics with the same name, and a scorecard that does not state the window cannot be compared to the year before it.
source: Standard definition; window is a stored decision rather than a derived one

measurement: Percent promoters minus percent detractors
use_when: Relationship-led categories where one survey question is all the customer will answer.
trap: Runs from -100 to +100, so a ratio breaks across zero: -10 against a target of 20 returns -50%, and -10 against a target of -20 returns +50%. Score it on a scale, never as actual/target.
source: Standard definition; the ratio failure follows directly from arithmetic and must be reviewed on a scale

measurement: Days from confirmed order to delivery
use_when: Operations objectives where the customer feels the delay before they see the quality.
trap: Averages hide the tail. Ten orders at three days and one at forty averages to six, and the one at forty is the complaint. Consider a percentile rather than a mean.
source: Direction taken from the guideline list of lower-is-better metrics in BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Guidelines

measurement: Orders delivered by promised date / orders delivered
use_when: Wholesale and B2B scorecards where the promise is the product.
trap: Improves when the promise gets looser. Read it beside lead_time or a team can hit it by quoting four weeks for everything.
source: Standard definition; pairing rule is a craft judgement

measurement: Date the agreement licence or certification is signed
use_when: One-off compliance and launch gates where the only question is whether it lands in time.
trap: The date branch is the scale branch on a day axis: earlier is better, so the rungs run later as achievement falls. Compare day ordinals, not strings — ISO dates happen to sort correctly as text and no other format does, so a string comparison is a bug that passes its first test. The source file stores these as Excel serials, which is why 45473 and not a date appears in the cell.

measurement: Count of standard operating procedures approved and published
use_when: Process-maturity objectives where the work is discrete and each item is a decision.
trap: A count of documents, not of adoption. It can be fully achieved by a folder nobody opens; pair it with a lagging process KPI.
source: Scale method inferred from comparable non-linear counts in BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet 2024

name_vi: Số nội dung xuất bản đúng lịch
measurement: Pieces published on the planned date / pieces planned
use_when: Content-engine scorecards where the failure mode is a calendar that quietly slips.
trap: Measures the calendar, not the work. A team can publish everything on time and move nothing, which is why it belongs in Processes and not in Customer.
source: Craft judgement; not present in the source file

measurement: Leavers in the period / average headcount
use_when: Any people aspect. It is the one number that shows up after the decisions that caused it.
trap: The file's own cascade example: company turnover under 20% is lagging and arrives too late to act on, so HR carries a happiness-survey score above 80% and a flexible-working launch date as its leading pair. A People aspect with only this KPI cannot be steered.
source: BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Guidelines — turnover rate < 20% cascaded to HR as two leading KPIs

measurement: Average score on the internal engagement survey
use_when: The leading half of a turnover objective
trap: cascaded to the team that can act on it.
evidence_grade: Self-reported and cheap to move with a good week. Store the response rate: a 90% score from a third of the company is a different number from a 90% score from all of it.
source: confirmed-fixture, BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Guidelines — happiness survey > 80% as the leading pair to turnover

measurement: Hours of training delivered per employee in the period
use_when: Capability-building objectives in a year where the skill gap is the stated constraint.
trap: A pure activity count, fully achievable while nothing changes. On its own it measures attendance; give it a lagging partner or drop it.
source: Named in the guideline list of leading indicators in BSC_2025_template.xlsx

measurement: Positions filled / positions in the approved plan
use_when: Growth years where the plan depends on hiring landing before the season.
trap: Filled is not started, and started is not productive. If the plan needs people working rather than signed, measure the start date instead.
source: Craft judgement; not present in the source file

name_vi: Mốc áp dụng làm việc linh hoạt
measurement: Date the flexible-working policy takes effect
use_when: Policy commitments cascaded down from a people objective
trap: where the date is the deliverable.
evidence_grade: A date KPI scores fully the moment it lands and then says nothing for the rest of the year. It belongs beside a KPI that keeps moving, not alone in the aspect.
source: confirmed-fixture, BSC_2025_template.xlsx sheet Guidelines — apply flexible working before 01/06 as a cascaded leading KPI
